front.text: Angličan Tom kupoval čerstvý chleb v trhu.

back.text: The English man Tom bought fresh bread at the market.
back.notes:
Angličan Tom kupoval čerstvý chleb v trhu

Angličan is the masculine singular noun indicating a male national from the United Kingdom, serving as the subject of the sentence.

[ˈeʃte raːs]

ešte raz is an adverbial phrase meaning once more or again, used here to request repetition of an action.

back.text: Mom, all right then, we're going now.
back.notes:
[tak ˈdɔbrɛ]

tak dobre is a discourse phrase expressing agreement or acceptance, meaning all right then or OK then.

front.text: Pozrite sa, tu je moja kniha.

back.notes:
[tu jɛ]

tu je is a presentational phrase: tu means here, and je is the third-person singular present form of byť, used to introduce something nearby.

back.text: Yes, I will come to the party.
back.notes:
[ˈaːno]

Áno is the affirmative particle meaning yes, used here to confirm an invitation or statement.

[ˈvɔŋku]

An adverb of place meaning “outside”; it indicates where the waiting happens.

front.text: V tiskom jsem zdieľal kufor s kolegom, ale on ho posielil do nového mesta.

back.text: I shared my suitcase with a colleague, but he sent it to a new city.
back.notes:
v tskim jsem zdieľal kufor s kolegom, ale on ho posielil do nového mesta.

kufor is the accusative form of 'kufor' (suitcase), serving as the direct object of the verb 'zdieľal' (shared).

front.text: Nemohla som to povedať tak dobre ako ty.

back.text: I couldn't say it as well as you.
back.notes:
[tak ˈdɔbrɛ]

Príslovcové spojenie „tak dobre“ znamená „tak veľmi dobre“; „tak“ zosilňuje príslovku „dobre“.

[ˈt͡ʃakaː]

čaká is the third-person singular present form of čakať, meaning is waiting; čakať na plus the accusative names the person or thing waited for.

front.text: Angličanka Lisa píše článok pre časopis.

back.text: The English woman Lisa writes an article for the magazine.
back.notes:
Angličanka Lisa píše článok pre časopis

Angličanka is the feminine singular noun indicating a female national from the United Kingdom, functioning as the subject of the sentence.

[samoˈzrei̯me]

Samozrejme is an adverb meaning of course, used here to emphasize certainty or obviousness.

[ja]

The personal pronoun “I” in the nominative singular, used as the emphasized subject.

[ˈʃɛst]

šest' is the cardinal number six in the nominative plural, agreeing with the plural noun jablk (apples).

front.text: Slovák Štefan kľúčom otvoril dve vrátania.

back.text: The Slovak Štefan opened two doors with a key.
back.notes:
Slovák Štefan kľúčom otvoril dve vrátania

Slovák is the nominative masculine singular noun denoting a person of Slovak ethnic origin, serving as the subject of the sentence.

tsikom

Discovered in: V tiskom jsem zdieľal kufor s kolegom, ale on ho posielil do nového mesta.

front.text: Slovenka Ana spravila na mieste konci knihy.

back.text: The Slovak woman Ana finished the book at the place.
back.notes:
Slovenka Ana spravila na mieste konci knihy

Slovenka is the feminine singular noun indicating a woman of Slovenian origin, functioning as the subject of the sentence.

[ˈpɔɟmɛ]

poďme is the first-person plural imperative form of ísť, used to suggest that the speaker and listener go together.

Mám novú auto.

auto is the noun denoting a motor vehicle, serving as the central topic of the sentence expressing possession.
